To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

aesthetic seascape values alone cannot account for attitudes to offshore wind farms, but that aesthetic perceptions of the local landscape are a significant factor in shaping attitudes to wind farm development.

local attitudes towards offshore wind farms are determined by three main aspects, namely: (1) aesthetic perception of the seascape, (2) local identity and landscape perception and (3) perceptions of renewable energy and related environmental issues.

local attitudes to offshore renewable energy are shaped by three factors: deeply held convictions about the sea as a space for nature, deeply held views about the local landscape as a place of local identity, and perceptions of renewable energy as part of climate change and sea-level rise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of aesthetic perceptions in shaping attitudes to offshore wind power development in the German EEZ.
the role of seascape values in the development of offshore wind power.
how local people experience the sea, and how this experience is related to their views on the development of wind farms in the sea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sea is a place where people can find peace and relaxation.
the sea is not a space for offshore wind farming in the sense that the local residents of the German North Sea coastal areas would like it to be.

aesthetic seascape values alone are not sufficient to explain local attitudes towards offshore wind farms, but rather that a number of other factors come into play, including deeply held views of nature, local identity and attitudes to climate change and sea-level rise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

aesthetic perceptions of seascape qualities are important for shaping local attitudes to large-scale wind farms in the North Sea, but that these attitudes are also shaped by a range of other factors, and that aesthetic perceptions of offshore wind farms may change as the wind farms become more familiar and as local attitudes to renewable energies change.
the local seascape is not only an important aspect for the development of the offshore wind power, it also plays a key role in the acceptance of this technology by local residents.
the sea is not just an energy space, but a place with a history, with a local landscape, a local seascape, and a local identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the future of the German North Sea as a natural space and as an energy space are closely linked.

local attitudes to offshore renewable energy development will depend on how the local seascape is perceived and on how this perception is shaped by other factors, such as local identities, views of climate change and sea-level rise.
local attitudes are not just about aesthetic values.
